verdict.rationale: Hatchet's own materials position it as an orchestration engine for AI agents and durable workflows, with automatic retries and durability built in, so the core of the story is the product's own capability. But the pack only has taglines and page titles. Nothing explicitly documents per-step checkpointing of model and tool calls or resuming an agent loop after a mid-run crash, and the founder notes that multi-step execution paths are declared ahead of time, which limits dynamic agent loops. Missing for 10: explicit docs on checkpointed LLM/tool-call steps, crash-recovery/resume semantics for agent loops, support for dynamic (non-predeclared) loop steps, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an agent builder, I run LLM agent loops as durable workflows — model and tool calls as checkpointed, retried steps that survive crashes mid-run

citations.quote: Hatchet is a platform for orchestrating background tasks, AI agents, and durable workflows at scale.
Hatchet provides a full platform for queuing, automatic retries, durability, real-time monitoring, alerting, and logging.
A single platform for orchestrating AI agents, scheduling background tasks, and running mission-critical workflows
